questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute pH of strong acid or base solutions
questions.stem: Sample 0901: What is the pH of a 0.0106 M solution of a strong monoprotic acid?

options.misconception: shifts the concentration by a factor of ten before taking the log
adds one pH unit without justification
drops the minus sign in the pH definition

questions.explanation: A strong monoprotic acid dissociates completely, so the hydrogen ion concentration equals the formal concentration. Taking the negative base-ten logarithm gives the pH, and any extra shift or sign error changes the result by a full unit or more.
questions.hint: Take minus the log of the concentration.

provenance.author: bank-team-analychem
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: estimate pH of a weak acid from Ka
questions.stem: Measurement 0902: A weak monoprotic acid has Ka = 1.77e-6 and concentration 0.059 M. Estimate the pH using the small-ionization approximation.

options.misconception: reports pOH after computing the acidic pH
uses the wrong power of concentration in the approximation
reports the pKa instead of the solution pH

questions.explanation: For a weak acid with small ionization the hydrogen concentration is approximately the square root of Ka times the formal concentration. The negative logarithm of that concentration is the pH. The pKa alone and the pOH are different quantities entirely.

provenance.author: bank-team-analychem
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute pH of strong acid or base solutions
questions.stem: Exercise 0903: Calculate the pH of a 0.0843 M solution of a strong monoprotic base?

options.misconception: shifts the concentration before converting
uses the wrong sign for pOH conversion
treats the strong base as if it were an acid

questions.explanation: A strong base dissociates completely, so pOH is the negative logarithm of the hydroxide concentration and pH equals fourteen minus pOH. Treating it as an acid or misapplying the sign gives a nonsensical acidic pH.

options.misconception: shifts the concentration by a factor of ten before taking the log
drops the minus sign in the pH definition
adds one pH unit without justification

questions.explanation: A strong monoprotic acid dissociates completely, so the hydrogen ion concentration equals the formal concentration. Taking the negative base-ten logarithm gives the pH, and any extra shift or sign error changes the result by a full unit or more.
questions.hint: Take minus the log of the concentration.

questions.stem: Record 0944: A weak monoprotic acid has Ka = 5.01e-4 and concentration 0.016 M. Estimate the pH using the small-ionization approximation.
